title: More oil for an already oiled head
literal_meaning: Oil on an already oiled head.
explanation: The extra oil goes where there is already oil. Used socially, the image questions giving still more attention, help or advantage to someone already well provided for, while others go without. It can sound wry or resentful, depending on who is speaking and how the benefit is being distributed.
meaning_odia: ଆଗରୁ ତେଲ ଥିବା ମୁଣ୍ଡରେ ପୁଣି ତେଲ ପଡ଼ୁଛି, ଆଉ ଯେଉଁଠି ଅଭାବ ସେଠି ନୁହେଁ। ସୁବିଧା ଓ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ବାରମ୍ବାର ଆଗରୁ ସୁବିଧା ପାଇଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ପାଖକୁ ଯିବାକୁ ଏହା ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରେ। କିଏ ଆଉ ପାଉଛି ମାତ୍ର ନୁହେଁ, କିଏ ବଞ୍ଚିତ ରହିଯାଉଛି ସେହି କଥା ବି ଭାବିବାକୁ ହୁଏ।
usage_example: A well-equipped group receives another set of supplies while a neighbouring group still lacks the basics. Someone uses the saying to question the allocation. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The head and oil remain the material image; no named oiling ritual, caste practice or historical incident is implied. The emphasis here is advantage being added to advantage. Other conversational uses, including praise directed at powerful people, need their own context rather than being treated as the only meaning.

odia_summary: ଯାହାର ଆଗରୁ ସୁବିଧା ଅଛି, ତାହାକୁ ହିଁ ଆଉ ଅଧିକ ସୁବିଧା ଦେବା। ଅନ୍ୟମାନଙ୍କ ଦରକାର ଅଣଦେଖା କରି ସେହି ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ବାରମ୍ବାର ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ବା ଆଦର ଦେଲେ ଏହି କଥାରେ ଅସନ୍ତୋଷ ପ୍ରକାଶ କରାଯାଏ।
english_summary: Attention or advantage goes to someone who already has plenty.
